current_leader.name: Adaptive synthetic-monitor frequency optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: fixed synthetic-check schedule -> real traffic/deployment/incident state changes -> current test cadence or geographic coverage becomes unnecessarily expensive -> recommend or apply a lower safe frequency/coverage -> preserve defined SLO/detection guardrails -> verify avoided billable test runs
current_leader.why_survived: Per-run synthetic pricing remains a direct recurring money meter, and current products expose configurable intervals/locations plus operational telemetry. Fresh exact-competitor searches did not find a product whose narrow commercial job is to continuously choose the minimum-cost safe test frequency and verify saved run spend. However, Kentik already auto-adjusts synthetic test locations using observed traffic and Datadog reviews expensive test setups, so adaptive synthetic configuration is an adjacent first-party/incumbent capability and Gate 8 is weaker than last run.
strongest_evidence: Datadog currently prices browser synthetics from $12 per 1,000 runs and API synthetics from $5 per 10,000 runs, making execution frequency a directly billable variable.
Independent 2026 synthetic-monitoring comparisons describe costs growing linearly with run volume and flag frequency/location multiplicative effects.
Finout explicitly recommends adjusting synthetic-check frequency and locations to control Datadog synthetic costs.
Kentik states that its synthetic service can use actual traffic to automatically configure and maintain tests and automatically adjust test locations when traffic flows change.

Site24x7 describes intelligent test scheduling based on historical data and predictive analytics as a direction for minimizing costs while preserving coverage, evidence that the optimization mechanism is technically credible but also absorbable by incumbents.
current_leader.closest_threat: Kentik already performs traffic-driven automatic adjustment of synthetic test locations; Datadog can identify expensive tests and has workflow automation plus cloud-cost automation primitives. The remaining whitespace is specifically automatic frequency optimization tied to a verified spend counterfactual, but incumbent absorption risk is material.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read synthetic definitions, run counts, real-user traffic, deploy/incident state and SLO constraints; compute minimum safe frequency per check; begin with recommendations, then optionally write schedule changes through vendor APIs. Keep a baseline-versus-optimized ledger and refuse changes that violate detection-latency/SLO policy.
current_leader.monetization: Per optimized monitor-month or capped share of verified avoided synthetic-run spend while reliability guardrails remain satisfied.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: The opportunity may self-limit because customers with obviously excessive high-frequency browser tests already have a strong incentive to tune them manually, while observability vendors can absorb adaptive scheduling into existing platforms.
current_leader.next_research_test: Search for evidence of real enterprise synthetic estates and billing pain, then quantify dynamic-versus-static savings using actual run-count distributions. In parallel, inspect Datadog/New Relic/Kentik/Checkly APIs and product roadmaps for automatic frequency mutation. Kill if dynamic savings beyond one-time manual tuning are small or if a first-party adaptive scheduler exists.

runner_ups.reason: General mechanism remains structurally strong but still lacks a better specific vertical than synthetics.
Very clean recovery attribution, but broad reconciliation software already finds missing refunds and leakage magnitude is still unproven.
Real app-store recovery economics, but infrequent app-wide configuration weakens recurring monetization and counterfactual measurement.

new_search_rules: Exact adaptive frequency remains distinct from traffic-driven adaptive test-location selection, but the latter is strong evidence of incumbent absorption risk.
A direct per-run price is not enough: prove incremental savings beyond a one-time static best-practice tuning exercise.
For observability wedges, compare the proposed optimizer against first-party workflow automation primitives, not just against explicit named cost-optimization features.
When a vendor can already inspect traffic and mutate one synthetic configuration dimension automatically, penalize adjacent dimensions even if the exact feature is absent.
